title: LAST SIGNAL
tagline: The desert keeps what you learn.
standingOrders: There is no work day. Every action costs clock time and fatigue. Tired hands are slow; exhausted hands are slower; at 100 fatigue you drop where you stand until dawn.
Midday sun kills in hours. Thirst, once empty, takes about two days. Hunger takes about four. Nothing empty kills you in a single tick.
Rest and sleep in shade or a shelter. Walking in the heat can burn two or three liters. A solar still makes half a liter to one liter a day. You want several.
Night halves your pace and wakes the things that bite. Fine work in the dark needs a fire or a torch. Rest, sleep, and waiting heal slowly, if you are fed, watered, and not bleeding.
Unknown plants can be eaten, ignored, or tested. The journal keeps the answer and brings it back next run. Your body does not.
Rescue has a hidden day between 18 and 25. A lit signal fire pulls that day earlier. Not every crash can be won.
opening: You come to on hot metal. The fuselage has opened like a seed pod. One wing is a black spine in the gravel. You are alive, which is a temporary fact.
There is no tower in your ear and no date on the rescue. If you die, the only thing you can send ahead is what you learned.
dawnLines: The metal ticks as the sun finds it.
Dawn is a gray mercy that will not last.
The horizon is a blade. Nothing on it is coming yet.
You wake with sand in your teeth and the same job as yesterday.
The sky is empty and very large.
Night lets go of the camp one degree at a time.

schematic.name: Solar still
schematic.text: A pit in low ground, a container at the bottom, a plastic sheet weighted so it drips, and tubing to drink without lifting the seal. One still yields about 0.5 to 1 liter a day. A wash placement yields more. One person needs about three.

nothingLog: Dust, rivets, and nothing you can carry.
knownFindLog: You know this one. {name}. The journal already argued with your hands.
journalPreface: Stats do not carry over. This does. Every entry was paid for by somebody, once.
